newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late but in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late but in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly lower late Monday despite a steady to firmer cash, but a lack of conviction about market direction kept prices in recent technical ranges, market sources said.
At 1355 EDT, July skidded 4.8 cents to $2.14 per million British thermal units, while August was 3.8 cents lower at $2.16. Most others were down by 0.2 to 3.3 cents.

"I'd be a little cautious about being long here. We get a couple of days of heat (in the Midwest and Northeast) this week, but the forecast is not that supportive," said a Midwest trader, noting cooler weather returns later in the week.

While eastern city gates firmed today because of forecasts for hotter midweek weather, most expected the gains to be short-lived, as seasonal to below-seasonal temperatures return to the region later in the week.
And with 6-10 day forecasts for the bulk of the nation calling for mostly below-normal weather, few expected a significant rally anytime soon.
But with spreads likely to encourage a decent pace of injections and partly offset the bearish weather patterns, they saw little reason for prices to move far in either direction.

Technical traders said the lack of conviction about market direction had many sidelined. They still saw support and resistance in July at $2.10 and $2.25, respectively. Stronger buying was expected at $2.08, with further resistance at $2.37 and then at the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, swing gas at the Louisiana Gulf firmed slightly Monday to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were little changed in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas gained about five cents on the heat to the mid-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 13,296 contracts traded at 1320 EDT.
On the KCBT, July fell 2.5 cents to $2.01, while deferreds were steady to 2.5 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.3 cents to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
